clue.text: Dignified death, hoarding old money

indicators.note: something hoarding keeps another thing stored inside it, so death's letters wrap the money

parts.note: death is the end of life
the noble was an old English gold coin

explanation.surface: A stately funeral where the deceased turns out to have been sitting on a pile of antique coins.
explanation.walkthrough: The old coin goes between the first two letters and the last letter of END.
explanation.definitionFit: To be raised to the nobility is to be dignified with rank; the past participle matches 'Dignified'.

clue.text: Junk TV harm: people wait to gain acceptance

indicators.note: to junk something is to scrap it, so these sixteen letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A grumble that viewers patiently put up with trashy, harmful television until it becomes normal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junk' looks like an adjective describing TV, but it is the anagram signal for the next four words.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: when something is received favourably it is said to gain acceptance among people.

clue.text: Solution offered by Australian state: cutting a rate of interest

indicators.note: cutting means the state's letters slice into the rate, sitting within it

parts.note: AER is the annual equivalent rate, a quoted rate of interest on savings
NSW is New South Wales

explanation.surface: A government in Australia offers a fix by reducing the interest rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the solution to a problem or puzzle is its reply or result.

clue.text: Writer takes every blockbuster film as movingly graceful

indicators.note: the writer takes the other pieces in, holding them inside

parts.note: a Bic is a ballpoint pen, something that writes
every one means all
ET, Spielberg's hit, is the blockbuster film

explanation.surface: An author regards every big Hollywood hit as gracefully moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancers in ballet are graceful in movement, so the adjective describes elegant motion.

clue.text: Shortening time before work on ground action

indicators.note: before puts the time letter first, ahead of what follows
on places the work piece next to the shuffled action, the two joined

parts.note: to run something, like a shop, is to work it

indicators.note: ground is broken down fine, so the word action is crushed into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions for a quick task done before the real business on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: cutting something short is curtailing it, the act of lopping off its end.

clue.text: "Extremely cold chest", Mark said

indicators.note: said means the words are spoken, and their sound gives the answer

parts.note: an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant; a tick is a mark of approval

explanation.surface: A man named Mark complains about a chest cold that feels bitterly icy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' poses as a person's name but is the tick.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar north is bitterly freezing, so the word describes anything intensely chilly.

clue.text: Conclude with army's opening invasion of Holland — hellish

parts.note: to infer is to conclude from evidence

indicators.note: invasion of means the army's letter goes inside the country's code

parts.note: NL is the international code for the Netherlands

indicators.note: opening means only the start of the word army's is used

explanation.surface: A war report on an army's first push into the Netherlands, ending in hellish scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: relating to the underworld, fiendish or devilish.

clue.text: Which should keep a worker from leaving wig off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters of leaving wig are mixed up

explanation.surface: A rule meant to stop a worker from leaving, or one whose wig has slipped off.
explanation.definitionFit: Pay high enough to support a basic standard of life is meant to sustain an employee.

clue.text: Atmospheric phenomenon or boomer sound?

indicators.note: sound tells us the pieces are heard aloud rather than read

parts.note: or is heraldic gold, chemical symbol AU, and a boomer is something that roars

explanation.surface: Asking whether a sky phenomenon is an atmospheric effect or a thunderous noise.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech AU ROAR, with a silent final R, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern or southern lights are glowing displays high in the sky.

clue.text: See 22
Given the law about dropping electric current, it might span two peaks

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters are rearranged
dropping says one letter falls out of the pool before rearranging

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: A physics conundrum about a law where the current is removed, spanning two peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: GIVEN THE LAW loses I and the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In a wave, the distance measured from one crest to the next is its defining length.

clue.text: Phone a spendthrift

definitions.meaning: British slang for the telephone, as in 'get on the dog and bone'
someone who blows money, spending it freely

explanation.definitionFit: British slang calls the telephone by this name; also one who squanders cash.

clue.text: Light weapon exploded after blast

indicators.note: after puts the shuffled weapon behind the blast

parts.note: a blast of wind

indicators.note: exploded means blown apart, so the word weapon is scattered

explanation.surface: A light gun blows up after an explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword sense: a light is a pane of glass in a window.

clue.text: Bird from Brazil? Mark with fine lines

parts.note: a Brazil is a nut, the large seed of a South American tree
to hatch is to shade with fine parallel lines

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher asks if a bird comes from Brazil, marked with delicate stripes.
explanation.definitionFit: A small songbird that climbs trees and cracks seeds open, as its name hints.

clue.text: Sort of dash into Ring dismissal

indicators.note: into means the dash goes inside the ring

parts.note: to dial a number is to ring it
an en dash is a printing dash the width of the letter N

explanation.surface: Someone rushing into a boxing ring only to be dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: refusing to accept or acknowledge something is rejecting it out of hand.

clue.text: See 2
Small creature has cold, rather than hot, stint

indicators.note: rather than says one letter stands where another was

parts.note: a shrimp is a small sea creature
H is the tap marking for hot
C is the tap marking for cold

explanation.surface: A tiny animal catches a chill instead of a fever and takes a short shift.
explanation.definitionFit: To stint is to be stingy or economise, to skimp on spending.

clue.text: £25 tip that could go to one's head

definitions.text: that could go to one's head

parts.note: in British slang a pony is twenty-five pounds
the tail is the tip or end of something

explanation.surface: A generous twenty-five pound gratuity that might make someone big-headed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go to one's head' suggests vanity but literally means worn at the back of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairstyle gathered at the back, so it sits on the head of whoever wears it.

clue.text: Teacher Patch turned over remains

indicators.note: turned over means the combined pieces are read from end to start

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
a patch of garden is a bed

explanation.surface: A teacher digs over a garden patch and finds what is left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the scattered fragments left after destruction.

clue.text: United, Poulenc incited divorce

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

indicators.note: incited means stirred up, so the composer's name is churned

explanation.surface: A couple who were united are driven to split by Poulenc's music.
explanation.walkthrough: Poulenc is a French composer; 'incited' turns his name into NCOUPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to detach or separate two things that were joined, as railway wagons.

clue.text: Retina mistaken for group of sea snails

indicators.note: mistaken means got wrong, so the letters of retina are rearranged

explanation.surface: An eye's retina is wrongly identified as a cluster of marine molluscs.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus of marine gastropods, a group of snail-like molluscs found on shores.

clue.text: Bar with two articles by tramp? It bears fruit

parts.note: to bar is to ban
AN and A are both indefinite articles
a tramp steamer is a cargo vessel with no fixed route

explanation.surface: A vagrant at a pub with a couple of items, suggesting something fruitful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tramp' poses as a vagrant but is a kind of ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel built to carry cargoes of tropical fruit, so it literally bears produce.

clue.text: Insect straddling overturned border soil

indicators.note: straddling means the insect's letters sit on either side of the edge

parts.note: a bee is an insect

indicators.note: overturned means the word for the edge is flipped round

parts.note: a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A bug sits astride an upturned flower border in the garden soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to cover or stain with mud, to dirty.

clue.text: Agent's message, maybe: "Try to come back between chapel and drive"

parts.note: a crypt is an underground chapel

indicators.note: to come back means the word for try is turned to read backwards

parts.note: to have a go is to try
to ram is to drive forcefully

explanation.surface: A quoted instruction urging someone to return between church and the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'try' piece is turned round by 'to come back'; 'chapel' fits because a crypt is a chapel below a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A coded text, like one sent by a secret agent, is an example of this.

clue.text: See 2
See 8
Laurel's sound, having a few lines?

indicators.note: sound tells us the possessive is heard aloud rather than read

parts.note: Stan Laurel was the thin half of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a comic actor's voice comes with a short script.
explanation.walkthrough: STAN'S followed by A is heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A verse of a poem is a group of a few lines set apart.

clue.text: Supervise "rag lion" housing for Muslim quarters

indicators.note: housing means the run of letters is held within the words supervise and rag lion

explanation.surface: An instruction to oversee a ragged lion kept in quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: The secluded women's quarters of a Muslim palace, such as the Ottoman harem.
